newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - April 4.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - April 4.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Friday:

* On Thursday, the Dow Jones industrial average fell 39.66 points to end at 6,477.35 amid lingering fears of rising U.S. interest rates, while all eyes were on Friday's report on payrolls, wages and unemployment for March, and the possible impact that the data might have on whether the Fed again raises interest rates.
* Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, has issued a new regulation which will tighten requirements to secure overseas loans for the local banking sector, Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported.
* Indonesia's foreign exchange reserves increased to $19.872 billion in March from $19.862 billion in February, a government official said on Thursday.
* Indonesia's Minister for Industry and Trade Tungky Ariwibowo said on Thursday the country posted a trade surplus of $575.4 million in January against $916.2 million in December.
* On Thursday, the Jakarta composite index fell 9.26 points, to close at 641.62 points.
* On Friday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,403.50/04.00 at 0130 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,404.50/05.50.
* Indofood after its shareholders approved the firm's 1.55 trillion rupiah proposed acquisitions of six firms in the Salim Group. The shareholders also approved a proposed 5:1 rights issue.
* Indocement after its shareholders approved a proposed purchase of 50.1 percent of subsidiary PT Indofood's rights issue.
* Second-liner Surya Semesta on market talk of a possible link-up with heavyweight cigarette maker Sampoerna.
* Ficorinvest Bank on market talk that several business tycoons were likely to take a large stake in the bank.
* Bank Lippo after announcement of a rise in its 1996 net profit.
